title: Henselian-pair comparison in degree zero
statement:
Let $(A,J)$ be a henselian pair, let $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper,
and let $i:Z_0=Z\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\hookrightarrow Z$. For every
sheaf of sets $F$ on $Z_{\Et}$, restriction is a bijection

$$
\Gamma(Z,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Gamma(Z_0,i^{-1}F).
$$

The comparison is natural in $F$.

In particular the theorem applies to sheaves of abelian groups and of
modules. It is Stacks Project, Tag 0A0C.

proof.text: Construct the quotient-spectrum map q and its pullback i. Surjectivity of the quotient homomorphism makes q a closed immersion, and base change makes i a closed immersion. Properness of f over the affine spectrum gives CompactSpace Z and QuasiSeparatedSpace Z. The pullback range formula and the range of the quotient-spectrum map identify range i with the inverse image of V(J).

For every finite h : X′ to Z the composite h followed by f is proper. Apply Scheme.Hom.isConnected_inter_preimage_zeroLocus, the connectedness clause of thm-weil-pbc-stein-inputs, to every irreducible closed subset C of X′. Using the range identity of step 1, this says C intersected with the inverse image of range i is nonempty and connected. This is the unit’s integral Stein-connectedness input, uniformly on all finite covers.

source.place: Tag 0A0B, integral Stein connectedness; Tag 0A0C, finite covers

proof.text: Apply zariski_closed_immersion_connected_restriction to i and to pullback.snd i h for every finite h. In each case use the connectedness of the closure of a singleton from step 2; pullback range_snd identifies the latter range with the inverse image of range i. Finite morphisms over Z have qcqs source. This gives exactly the Type (u+1)-valued Zariski unit hypotheses of Gabber’s criterion, avoiding the smaller-universe interface of zariski_h0_proper_henselian_pair.

source.place: Tag 09ZG, spectral closed restriction; universe-compatible library specialization

proof.text: Apply gabber_h0_etale_criterion with these two Zariski unit hypotheses. Its conclusion is bijectivity of the set inverse-image unit evaluated at the identity etale object. The second factor in henselianPairH0SetRestriction is the presheaf image of an isomorphism, hence is an isomorphism of sets and a bijection. Compose the two bijections.

Evaluate naturality of the set inverse-image adjunction unit at the identity etale object. Compose this equation with the terminal-object transport in henselianPairH0SetRestriction. Naturality of the inverse-image sheaf morphism along that transport identifies the resulting composite with the displayed naturality equality. The Lean proof uses only congrArg, associativity, and NatTrans.naturality.

source.place: Adjunction unit naturality and presheaf morphism naturality

These are precisely the final two conjuncts, without any change of their restriction maps or sheaf encodings.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $(A,J)$ be a henselian pair, let $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper,
and let $i:Z_0=Z\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\hookrightarrow Z$. For every
sheaf of sets $F$ on $Z_{\Et}$, restriction is a bijection

$$
\Gamma(Z,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Gamma(Z_0,i^{-1}F).
$$

The comparison is natural in $F$. In particular the same holds for every sheaf
of abelian groups, or of $\Lambda$-modules, on $Z_{\Et}$.

proof.text:
The geometric content is a connectedness statement: every irreducible closed
subset of a scheme proper over a henselian pair meets the closed fibre in a
nonempty connected subset. Stein factorization and henselian connectedness
prove this (Stacks Project, Tag 0A0B), and spectral-space restriction then
gives equality of sections for Zariski sheaves. The connectedness statement
also holds after every finite cover, since that cover remains proper over
$A$. A finite surjection whose Zariski-local pieces factor through the étale
covering, followed by descent on its self-intersection, upgrades the Zariski
comparison to étale sheaves (Stacks Project, Tag 09ZF). Over a general affine
base the integral form of Stein factorization, whose algebra need not be
finite, suffices for this argument. This is Stacks Project, Tag 0A0C.

For sheaves of abelian groups or of $\Lambda$-modules, apply the statement to the
underlying sheaf of sets. Forgetting the algebraic structure commutes with
$\Gamma$ and with $i^{-1}$, since it preserves finite limits and filtered
colimits, and it reflects isomorphisms.
